newsitem.title: CUBA: Castro opens French bakery in Havana.
newsitem.headline: Castro opens French bakery in Havana.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro on Thursday formally opened a small factory that caused an enthusiastic stir among foreign residents in Havana -- a bakery producing French bread and croissants.

Castro, accompanied by members of a visiting group of French entrepreneurs, praised the pristine premises and the quality of production at the Cuban-French owned Francuba bakery, the Cuban official news agency Prensa Latina said.
Francuba is operated by Cuban state firm Cubanacan and a Marseille-based French firm, Cofeco International. It opened for business several weeks ago.

The bakery sells French long thin loaves called baguettes and a variety of other breads until now unavailable in Havana, as well as croissants and other pastries. It quickly attracted customers among foreign residents of the Cuban capital.
Francuba's product joins the baguettes produced by Francesa del Pan, another Cuban state firm in Havana operating in association with a French firm, Moulins Dumee SA.
In both cases, the bread is sold in hard currency, putting it out of range of most Cubans, who either have only pesos or earn far too few dollars to spend them on the relative luxury of good bread.

Castro told Francuba executives to be sure to maintain the quality of their product, saying competition loomed as several Cuban state enterprises were starting to produce French-style bread and pastries.

The Francuba bakery has capacity to produce some 2.5 metric tons of bread a day and its product is aimed principally at the 18,000 foreigners who live in Cuba as well as the tourism market, Prensa Latina said.
Thursday's formal opening took place during a week-long visit by a French trade mision that ends on Saturday.
